notes: Everything is in rounds/tester.py's result view (GET and POST, the POST under the round lock): it refuses Closed rounds and superseded builds, reads only the signed-in tester's result, refuses a POST to a submitted result and passes `submitted` to the template, which then shows no form; the write is an update_or_create keyed on the signed-in tester. M1 drops the tester filter and keys the write on the found result's tester, so another tester's result is shown and overwritten; M3 leaves the tester round page's Open-only 'Record result' link in place (navigation, not a guard); M4 sets `submitted` to False, removing the POST guard and the read-only view in one edit (the status line still shows Submitted). ResultForm.clean requires a Fail observation (no database constraint backs it) and BrowserTextField(max_length=2000) limits it with an explicit message, which M5 leaves saying 2,000. M5 also widens the model field and its column in migration 0005 to 2001, together, because the varchar(2000) column would otherwise refuse the save (a 503) and a model-only change would fail the candidate's makemigrations --check test; pytest-django builds the test database from migrations on every run (no --reuse-db), so the migration edit is seen consistently.
